## 08/10/2026 12:56 — Yes, That Is ChatGPT Advertising

Yes, partner. **That banner is inviting *you* to become an advertiser on ChatGPT.** It isn't merely advertising another company to you.

Your screenshot says:

> **“Create your first ChatGPT ad in minutes”**\
> “Add your website URL, review your suggested ad, and launch…”

OpenAI now has a self-serve **Ads Manager** where businesses can create campaigns, set budgets/bids, upload ads and measure performance. 

### Is it basically Google Ads?

**Broadly yes — but the placement/matching model is interestingly different.**

Google Ads is heavily search/keyword driven. ChatGPT Ads can appear when someone is **having a relevant conversation, exploring alternatives, comparing products, or making a decision**. Advertisers can provide “context hints” about relevant conversations/topics/keywords, but they aren't exact-match keywords. 

Current buying supports **CPM/impressions and CPC/clicks**, with conversion optimization/measurement as well. OpenAI currently recommends roughly **$3–$5 maximum CPC as a starting point**, although actual auction pricing varies. 

And the advertiser page currently shows a promotion:

> **Spend $500 → get $500 ad credit.** 

### This is actually relevant to our earlier product-distribution problem

You previously constrained yourself against traditional sales/outreach and were looking at marketplace + SEO distribution.

This creates a **new distribution channel we hadn't had before**:

`Someone asks ChatGPT:  "I need software to analyse customer support calls"                     ↓              relevant ad auction                     ↓               Your product ad                     ↓                landing page                     ↓                  signup`

Not guaranteed placement, of course. But it's fundamentally different from hoping someone discovers an SEO article months later.

OpenAI says advertisers **do not receive users' conversations or personal details**; they get aggregate campaign/performance information. Ads are also supposed to remain separate from and not influence ChatGPT's answer. 

One oddity in **your screenshot**: you're on Plus, and OpenAI's current help material says Plus users aren't supposed to *receive* ads.  But this banner looks like an **advertiser-acquisition promotion** (“start advertising”), rather than a normal sponsored result targeted at you as a consumer. So those two things aren't necessarily contradictory.

**I would not spend money on this now.** But when we return to your product distribution work, ChatGPT Ads should absolutely go into the channel map alongside marketplace, SEO, communities, and other paid acquisition channels. ## 08/10/2026 13:29 — ChatGPT Ads Baseline

Yes, partner. **This is now the baseline for this separate page.**

I’ll keep the Sarvam investigation out of here. This page is specifically for **ChatGPT Ads as a potential product-distribution channel**.

One important thing before we build conclusions on the pasted answer: some claims there are quite specific — **$3–$5 CPC, CPM/CPC buying, context hints, $500 credit, availability and targeting mechanics**. Because this is new and changing quickly, I would **verify each of those against the current official OpenAI Ads/Help documentation before treating them as facts or making a spending decision**.

## 08/10/2026 13:35 — Yes, Similar to YouTube Premium

**Yes — that is a good analogy.**

Think of it roughly like this:

| Platform | Ad-supported users | Ad-free subscribers |
|---|---|---|
| YouTube | Normal/free users see ads | Premium subscribers don't |
| ChatGPT | **Free + Go** may see ads | **Plus / Pro / Business / Enterprise / Edu don't** |

OpenAI explicitly confirms that Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu accounts are ad-free. citeturn0search2turn0search0

There is actually an even closer analogy now: **Free ChatGPT users can choose an ad-free Free experience, but they receive lower usage limits and reduced feature access.** citeturn0search7

### But this creates our B2B problem

YouTube advertisers accept losing Premium viewers because the remaining ad-supported audience is enormous.

ChatGPT has the same broad logic:

**Ads subsidise Free/low-cost access; subscriptions buy an ad-free experience.** citeturn0search3

But **for our enterprise products**, the audience we're most interested in may disproportionately be using:

> Business / Enterprise / Plus / Pro → **no ads**

So the crucial question isn't whether ChatGPT Ads has a huge audience—it does. OpenAI says ChatGPT now has **more than 1 billion weekly active users**. citeturn0search4

The question is:

> **What percentage of the people who can actually buy our enterprise software are reachable through the ad-supported Free/Go audience?**

We don't have evidence yet that this percentage is high.

So I would treat **ChatGPT Ads much like YouTube Ads: potentially enormous reach, but not automatically the right audience for an enterprise SaaS sale.**

That's the distinction we should preserve when we later evaluate it against **Google Search Ads, marketplaces, SEO, partner ecosystems and enterprise sales.**

## 08/10/2026 13:28 — ChatGPT Ads Distribution

Yes, partner. **Keep this as a separate page/thread.** The ChatGPT advertising discussion started accidentally inside the Sarvam thread, and it is a different topic.

### Context carried into this page

The screenshot shows an advertiser-acquisition banner:

> **“Create your first ChatGPT ad in minutes”**  
> Add your website URL → review the suggested ad → launch.

The question for this page is **not merely “what is this banner?”** We should investigate ChatGPT Ads as a possible **distribution channel for our products**, including:

**Product → ChatGPT Ads → relevant user conversation → click → landing page → signup → paid customer**

The important questions are cost/CPC/CPM, targeting and conversation matching, geographic availability, eligibility, conversion tracking, advertiser controls, whether there is genuinely a $500 credit offer, and—most importantly—**whether this could realistically acquire customers for any of our products without direct outreach**.

I would keep **Sarvam API/Cowork/LLM/voice-agent investigation in the original Sarvam page** and continue all ChatGPT advertising investigation here.

## 08/10/2026 13:33 — Paid Users & Sponsored Search

**No. At present, it does *not* work like Google sponsored search across paid ChatGPT users.**

If I am on **Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu** and ask:

> “What are the best AI call-quality platforms for an enterprise contact centre?”

your paid ChatGPT advertisement **cannot be inserted into my results**. OpenAI explicitly says those plans do **not** receive ads. citeturn0search0turn0search2

Google is different:

```text
GOOGLE

Free Google user ────────┐
                         ├─ Search "call centre QA software"
Paid/Workspace user ─────┘
                              ↓
                       Sponsored results
                              ↓
                         Our product
```

Whereas currently:

```text
CHATGPT

Free ───────┐
Go ─────────┼── Relevant conversation
            │          ↓
            │      Sponsored ad
            │          ↓
            │      Our product
            │
Plus ───────┐
Pro ────────┤
Business ───┤── ❌ NO ADS
Enterprise ─┤
Edu ────────┘
```

OpenAI also makes an important distinction: **buying an ad does not buy ranking inside ChatGPT's answer.** Ads are separate from the model response and appear below it; advertisers cannot pay to shape, rank or alter the answer. citeturn0search2

### So this makes your enterprise concern stronger

Imagine a CTO on **ChatGPT Enterprise** searches:

> “Compare the best enterprise voice QA platforms.”

We **cannot pay OpenAI to put TalkProof at #1, #2 or #3** in that answer.

That's fundamentally unlike Google Search Ads.

The only way our product gets into that organic ChatGPT answer is because ChatGPT's retrieval/model considers it relevant—not because we paid for advertising.

And there is an interesting future development: OpenAI is testing **Sponsored Agents**, where someone can open an ad and actually converse with an AI representative of the advertiser. But that's currently a **limited alpha for selected advertisers**, not generally available. citeturn0search16

### My revised channel view

For our **enterprise products**, this makes:

**Google Search Ads potentially more directly valuable than ChatGPT Ads** for capturing enterprise buyers with explicit purchase intent, because ChatGPT's most valuable paid/business audience is deliberately excluded from advertising.

ChatGPT Ads could still be useful for **SMB/self-service versions** of our products.

That distinction should stay on this page because it materially changes the commercial case for us.

## 08/10/2026 13:31 — ChatGPT Ads: Enterprise Problem

Yes. **Your objection is the important one**, and it changes how much value I assign to ChatGPT Ads for our products.

First, I'll preserve the facts we have established on this page.

### What ChatGPT Ads currently are

| Area | Current position |
|---|---|
| Who sees ads | **Free + Go users** |
| Who does **not** see ads | **Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu** |
| Placement | Below a ChatGPT answer, clearly marked sponsored |
| Matching | Conversation context/intent + landing page + ad copy + advertiser “context hints”; personalization can add broader signals |
| Keywords | Context hints can contain topics/keywords, but **not Google-style exact-match keywords** |
| Objectives | Views, Clicks, Conversions |
| Charging | CPM or CPC depending on campaign/objective |
| Suggested starting max CPC | **$3–$5** for CPC campaigns |
| Targeting | Geography, platform and custom audiences are available, subject to account/region restrictions |
| Measurement | Impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, CPM, conversions; Pixel/Conversions API available |
| UK | Ads launched in the UK in August 2026 |
| Intro offer | Current advertiser page says **spend $500 → get $500 ad credit** |
| Privacy | Advertisers don't receive the user's conversations/personal details |
| Influence on answer | **None.** Paying doesn't make ChatGPT recommend the product |
| Your screenshot | An invitation for you to **become an advertiser**, not a normal sponsored product ad |

These points are now confirmed against current OpenAI documentation. citeturn0search0turn0search1turn0search2turn0search3

urlOpenAI ChatGPT Ads Managerturn0search2

---

# But your enterprise objection is correct

Suppose we sell something like TalkProof to:

**Head of Contact Centre → QA Director → CTO → Enterprise Architect → Procurement**

There are two very different situations.

### Situation A — they use their corporate ChatGPT

```text
Enterprise decision maker
        ↓
ChatGPT Enterprise / Business
        ↓
"Find tools for analysing 100,000
customer-service calls per month"
        ↓
ChatGPT answer
        ↓
❌ OUR AD CANNOT APPEAR
```

Business and Enterprise accounts are explicitly ad-free. citeturn0search0

That's a **major limitation for B2B enterprise acquisition**.

### Situation B — the same person researches privately

```text
Contact-centre director
        ↓
Personal ChatGPT Free / Go
        ↓
"We need to automate QA for
our call centre..."
        ↓
Conversation signals commercial intent
        ↓
TalkProof-type advertisement
        ↓
Landing page
        ↓
Demo / trial / contact
```

**That person can potentially see our advertisement.**

And OpenAI itself specifically gives **“choosing software for their business”** as an example of the kind of decision people make in ChatGPT. citeturn0search4turn0search5

So Free ≠ only students or low-value consumers.

A founder, consultant, developer, small-business owner or enterprise employee can use a Free/Go personal account.

But we **cannot assume enough enterprise buyers behave this way**.

---

# There is another problem for us

OpenAI's current advertising policy says its early advertising categories are focused on areas including consumer goods, local services, travel/entertainment, **digital products and education**. Categories are expected to expand. citeturn0search9

Therefore I would **not yet assume every complex enterprise SaaS product in our portfolio is eligible or will receive useful inventory.**

That's something we'd test rather than infer.

---

# Where I think ChatGPT Ads fit for us

This changes my earlier assessment.

For a **£50k–£500k enterprise sale**, I would **not make ChatGPT Ads our primary acquisition strategy**.

But consider a product that can be bought without enterprise procurement:

```text
Free ChatGPT user
       ↓
"I need to merge 300 Google Docs"
       ↓
DocMerge Pro ad
       ↓
£29/month signup
```

or:

```text
Shopify merchant
       ↓
"How do I reduce customer churn?"
       ↓
RetainKit ad
       ↓
Shopify install
```

or:

```text
Small support-team manager
       ↓
"How can AI score my support calls?"
       ↓
TalkProof ad
       ↓
Free trial
```

**Those are much more interesting.**

Therefore, across our product portfolio I'd initially think:

**Self-serve / SMB product → potentially strong experiment**

**Mid-market product → possible lead-generation experiment**

**Enterprise-only product → secondary channel, not the core distribution mechanism**

---

## And this exposes something bigger

We have repeatedly framed our products as **enterprise-grade**.

That does **not necessarily mean the customer has to be enterprise-only**.

We can have:

```text
                    PRODUCT

        Enterprise-grade architecture
                    │
        ┌───────────┼────────────┐
        ↓           ↓            ↓
   Individual      SMB       Enterprise
    £20–£50      £100–500    £20k–£200k+
       │            │             │
 ChatGPT Ads   Marketplace     Enterprise
 Marketplace   ChatGPT Ads       sales/
     SEO           SEO           partners
```

That is potentially much more important than merely discovering another advertising platform.

Our earlier distribution problem may partly come from repeatedly building **enterprise-capable software and then thinking only about enterprise-style distribution**.

ChatGPT Ads could be useful **if we deliberately expose a self-service entry point into the same product**.

And OpenAI now explicitly says SMBs/startups make up a material share of its advertiser base, while the platform supports conversion optimisation and measurement. citeturn0search5

So I would **keep ChatGPT Ads on our distribution map, but not conclude yet that it solves enterprise distribution.** Your Free/Go observation is exactly why we shouldn't jump from *“new ad channel”* to *“solution to our customer problem.”*

When we return to the 12-product commercial review, **this should become a new column: “ChatGPT Ads suitability: High / Medium / Low + buyer path.”**
